name: Finalize NFR (Not For Resale) country setup
description: Post-open-country finalizer for NFR mode: verify the international shipping profile, confirm import-duty disclosure at checkout, spot-check product country-of-origin labeling, and run a light compliance review acknowledging the NFR posture. Expects the caller `context` from open-country PLUS `mode: "nfr"`.

steps.name: International shipping profile
steps.prompt:
NFR means the customer imports the product cross-border — every NFR country needs a shipping rate at checkout, or the shopper has no shipping option for their address. Fluid has no shipping-zone API: the company picks ONE shipping pricing option for the whole store (Settings > Commerce > Shipping), and coverage for a country depends on that option.

1. Read `context.country_id`, `context.mode` (should be `nfr`), and `context.country_iso` (or resolve via GET /api/countries) from the context block. If mode is not `nfr`, emit `STEP_OUTPUT: mode is not nfr; nothing to do` and STOP.
2. Read the store's shipping option: `fluid_api` → GET `/api/settings/companies/{id}` (the company's own id) and read `shipping_type`: `manual` (Product-based Rates), `country` (Flat Country Rates), `droplet`, `fluid-rates`, or `free-shipping`.
3. Check coverage for this country, read only:
   a. `fluid-rates` — GET `/api/v2025-06/shipping_methods?status=active`. The country is covered when an active method has a `shipping_method_rates` tier whose `country === context.country_iso`, or has only Global tiers (no `country`) — a method's Global tiers stop applying once it has any country-specific tier.
   b. `country` — GET `/api/settings/company_countries` and read this country's shipping/handling fee (`base_shipping` / `handling_fee`). A missing fee means checkout charges nothing for shipping there; report it.
   c. `manual` — rates live on each variant's `variant_countries` entry for the country (its `shipping`). Spot-check 3 active products via GET `/api/v202604/company/products/{id}` and report whether the entry under `context.country_iso` has a shipping rate.
   d. `droplet` or `free-shipping` — the droplet or free shipping answers for every country; report it as covered and name the option.
4. If the country is covered, report `already covered by <option> (<method name or detail>)` and STOP. Otherwise emit a manual step — shipping methods need a warehouse and rate tiers a human must choose, so don't create one: `SETUP REQUIRED: in the admin, open Settings > Commerce > Shipping (/settings/shipping) and add a rate for <country> under the store's shipping option (for Fluid Rates, a tier for <country> on an active shipping method).`
5. STEP_OUTPUT names the shipping option and the resolution: already-covered / manual-step-emitted.
acceptance: The report names the store's shipping option, read this turn from `shipping_type` on GET /api/settings/companies/{id}, and the read that showed whether context.country_iso is covered under it (an active shipping method's tier, the country's shipping/handling fee, or variant shipping rates), OR a manual follow-up naming Settings > Commerce > Shipping.
STEP_OUTPUT reports which branch ran: already-covered | manual-step-emitted — no silent success.

steps.name: Import-duty disclosure check
steps.prompt:
NFR without an import-duty disclosure at checkout leads to customs surprises and chargebacks. The storefront MUST tell the buyer that import duties/taxes may apply and are paid on delivery.

1. Read `context.country_id` and `context.country_iso` from the context.
2. Crawl the public storefront's checkout / cart page and one product detail page. Use `run_cli fluid theme crawl <url> --format markdown,screenshot --viewport 1440x900 --evidence .`, then open the saved screenshot (`evidence.path`) with `view_project_image`. Locate the storefront URL via GET /api/settings/companies/{id} or from an earlier step's STEP_OUTPUT.
3. Search the crawled markdown for import-duty language — case-insensitive match on any of: 'import dut', 'customs dut', 'may apply on delivery', 'paid by the recipient', 'DDU', 'delivered duty unpaid', 'buyer is responsible for'.
4. If found, record `import-duty disclosure present at <page url>` with the matched sentence.
5. If NOT found, produce a specific fix instruction: recommend adding a short paragraph to the checkout page and the product page footer for shipments to this country. Draft ONE sentence the human can drop in, in the country's primary language (the `languageCode` from `run_cli fluid countries compliance <iso>` — English fallback when not curated). Example draft: 'Orders shipped to <country> may be subject to import duties and taxes on delivery, paid by the recipient.'
6. STEP_OUTPUT names the pages checked, the search terms tried, and the resolution (present | fix-required).
acceptance: At least one storefront page (checkout and/or product detail) was crawled THIS turn — the report includes the URL and either the matched disclosure sentence OR a note that no match was found.
If no disclosure is found, the report includes a concrete one-sentence draft in the country's primary language (or English fallback) that a human can paste into the theme.
STEP_OUTPUT lists the pages checked and the search terms used so the compliance review can pick up the finding.

steps.name: Product labeling spot check
steps.prompt:
Even though NFR imports fall on the buyer for most consumer-protection duties, the physical products themselves still need to comply with the destination's minimum labeling — country-of-origin marking on the goods, and (for many countries) English-language or destination-language labels on consumer goods regardless of the local language.

1. GET `/api/company/v1/products?per_page=3` for a spot-check sample (three active products is enough).
2. For each product, check the product record for a `country_of_origin` field (either directly on the product or on any variant). Report present/absent per product.
3. If the product record has photos, look at the primary image via `web_fetch` — is a country-of-origin label visible on the packaging? This is best-effort; a null answer is acceptable.
4. Read `languageCode` from `run_cli fluid countries compliance <iso>` — most non-English-primary countries still require English labels for imported consumer goods (an EU regulatory floor + national conventions in JP, MX, etc.). Note whether the sample's labeling appears to satisfy that.
5. STEP_OUTPUT: per-product `country_of_origin: present | absent | unknown`, and a summary line like `2/3 products missing country_of_origin — human must add before shipping to <country>`.
acceptance: Three products were spot-checked via GET /api/company/v1/products; the report names each by id and records `country_of_origin: present | absent | unknown`.
The report includes a one-line labeling summary and, when items are missing, a follow-up item that names how many products need country-of-origin added before shipping to this country.

steps.name: Light NFR compliance review
acceptance: A compliance report was produced with an explicit NFR-posture note in the summary — most consumer-facing website obligations are graded at a lower bar because the buyer imports the goods, and the report says so plainly.
Findings from the earlier NFR-specific steps (import-duty disclosure, country-of-origin labeling) appear in the report with severity assigned.
Every finding cites a specific rule from `fluid countries compliance <iso>` or, for NFR-specific findings, cites the earlier workflow step whose spot check produced it.
